title: Offer Acceptance Welcome Sprint and Skill Transfer Map
content:
Purpose:
To stitch together a short, operational 'welcome sprint' that takes a candidate from offer acceptance to first-30-days evidence portfolio and creates a repeatable skill-transfer handoff for managers and teams. This is designed for fast-moving IC hires, contract-to-perm conversions, and high-priority headcount where time-to-impact matters.

Scope and audience:
- People Ops partner and onboarding coordinator (primary)
- Hiring manager (owns role-specific ramp)
- Hiring panel / interviewers (for final rubrics & handoff notes)
- New hire / candidate (receives tailored checklist)

Quick summary of flow (offer -> D30 -> D90):
- Offer accepted (Day -7 to Day 0): paperwork, equipment, manager intro, first-week agenda sent
- Day 0: account access + orientation + buddy pairing + 30/60/90 expectations
- Week 1 (D1–D7): setup, team syncs, micro-project assigned (non-blocking), 1:1 with manager 2x
- Weeks 2–4: role-specific ramp, ownership of small deliverable, 30-day evidence review
- Month 2: broader cross-team context + measurable output (ticket, doc, small feature)
- Month 3: 90-day recommendation (pass/go-forward + next-sprint objectives)

Day -7 to Day -1 (offer acceptance checklist - outbound tasks):
- HR sends welcome packet + employment paperwork + benefits enrollment links (Owner: People Ops)
- Equip request placed in IT (specify GPU/monitor/hardware if applicable); cc hiring manager (Owner: Hiring Manager + IT)
- Slack workspace invite, calendar hold for Day 0 orientation, team all-hands invite (Owner: People Ops)
- Manager shares 2-page role-context doc and short reading list (Owner: Hiring Manager)
- Assign onboarding buddy and intro email drafted (Owner: People Ops)
- Quick risk check: expiration of background checks, VISA needs, KMS/HSM onboarding timeline for Private customers (Owner: People Ops & Security)

Day 0 (orientation - check as finished):
- Welcome call with People Ops (30m): payroll, benefits, org chart, intro to People Ops contact
- Team welcome: 20m team intro + 1:1 intros scheduled for first 2 weeks
- Tools access: GitHub org, Redwood internal docs, Confluence, JIRA/Linear, CI dashboards, Console demo creds (Owner: IT + Eng Onboarding)
- Buddy check-in scheduled daily for week 1

Week 1 (setup + micro-project):
- Micro-project assigned (should be deliverable in 3–7 days, low-risk): examples: small bugfix, doc draft, mini-integration test, or onboarding eval prompt set (Owner: Hiring Manager)
- Interviewer rubrics & final feedback packet delivered to manager (see Rubric Snapshot below)
- First-week 1:1s: Day 2 (buddy), Day 3 (manager), Day 7 (manager)

Skill Transfer Map (to be attached as objective-based checklist per role):
- Identify top 4 role skills (example for Serving Runtime SWE):
  1) Latency profiling & perf tooling: evidence = run benchmark + short postmortem
  2) Kernel selection & build debugging: evidence = reproduce a regression & propose fix
  3) Model versioning & rollouts: evidence = write runbook for a safe rollback
  4) Observability traces + tracing hooks: evidence = instrument a route and capture an error mode
- For each skill include: current assessment (hiring panel notes), target metric (what success looks like at D30/D90), 30-day artifact (doc/code/test), owner for mentorship

30-day evidence checklist (manager + people ops review):
- Micro-project completed and available in repo or doc
- 30-day 1:1 notes with explicit learning goals recorded
- Evidence artifacts attached to candidate file (links + short summary)
- Manager gives preliminary "on-track" / "needs support" signal (written)
- People Ops runs a pulse survey with hire about ramp blockers

Interview Rubric Snapshot (to be completed by final interviewers and forwarded to manager):
- Technical Fundamentals (0–4): core algorithmic/architecture understanding
- Problem Solving (0–4): structured approach, tradeoffs, ability to triage
- System Design / Scale (0–4): relevant for backend/infra roles
- Ownership & Communication (0–4): async clarity, cross-team collaboration examples
- Role-fit / Impact (0–4): examples of past work mapping to this role
- Summary notes (short paragraph): unresolved gaps, areas to mentor first 30 days, score rationale
- Recommendation field: "strong hire" / "hire" / "consider with caution" / "no hire"

Manager Handoff Template (to attach to onboarding folder):
- Final candidate summary (1 paragraph)
- Top 3 strengths and 2 risk areas (explicit)
- Skills to prioritize first 30 days (linked to Skill Transfer Map)
- Micro-project description + acceptance criteria
- Access list & blocked services expected to be needed (include KMS/HSM/Private infra notes)
- Suggested Mentor/Buddy contact list

People Ops operational notes / checklist items (internal):
- Use this doc as the canonical welcome sprint for offers tagged: "fast-track" or "contract-to-perm"
- Add candidate to fast-track tracker sheet (link in linked_artifacts)
- Escalation: if equipment not delivered by Day -1, create ticket with people-ops escalation tag and notify hiring manager + SRE (timeline target: 48 hours)
- Data capture: store 30 & 90 day signals in HRIS (for quality-of-hire metrics)

Open questions / TBD (notes to self):
- Should we standardize micro-project templates per team (templates exist but adoption inconsistent)?
- How to encode VARIANCE for on-call ramp (some infra roles need limited on-call at D30; others later)
- Do we require manager sign-off on evidence artifacts in Confluence or is a note in HRIS sufficient?

Quick links & templates (copy & paste):
- Micro-project template: confluence:ONBOARD-6321/micro-project-template
- Manager handoff doc template: gdrive:shared_drives/company/misc/manager-handoff-template
- Candidate welcome email sample: gdrive:shared_drives/company/misc/candidate-welcome-email-sample

Action items (next 7 days):
- [People Ops] Finalize welcome email variants for remote vs on-site hires (Owner: Aisha)
- [Hiring Manager] Prepare micro-project and acceptance criteria before Day 0 (Owner: manager)
- [IT] Confirm equip staging and shipping SLA for EMEA hires (Owner: IT Ops)
- [DevEx] Build short video tour of Redwood Console for new hires (Owner: DevEx)

Notes on tone & candidate experience:
- Keep communications time-boxed and specific (candidate should always know "what's next" within 24 hours)
- Avoid heavy admin during Day 0; prefer split orientation + small async tasks
- For contract-to-perm conversions, capture prior work artifacts as part of 30-day evidence to speed decisioning

Revision history:
- 2026-02-15 Aisha: initial draft
- 2026-02-20 Jon: added rubric snapshot + micro-project guidance
- 2026-02-28 Maya: clarified equipment escalation and added linked templates

End of document.
